watering: Water deeply 2–3 times a week when the top 1–2 inches of soil feel dry. Water the base, not foliage.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6–8 hours of direct daily sunlight.
soil: Well-drained, fertile loamy soil with pH 6.0–6.8 and rich organic compost.
fertilizer: Balanced 10-10-10 early on; high potassium and phosphorus during fruiting every 2 weeks.
pruning: Pinch suckers in leaf axils and remove yellowing bottom foliage for ventilation.
common_problems: Early blight, blossom end rot (calcium deficiency), hornworms, leaf curl from uneven water.

watering: Water consistently; keep soil evenly moist (about 1–2 inches per week). Reduce watering when foliage yellows.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6+ hours of direct sunlight.
soil: Loose, well-aerated sandy loam with pH 5.0–6.0. Hill up soil over growing tubers.
fertilizer: Low nitrogen, higher phosphorus and potassium (5-10-10) every 3 weeks.
pruning: No heavy pruning needed. Hill soil 6–8 inches high around stems as plants grow.
common_problems: Late blight, potato beetles, scab disease, green tubers from sun exposure.

watering: Water 1–2 inches per week; keep soil moist but never soggy. Allow surface to dry slightly.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6–8 hours of direct warm sunlight.
soil: Well-draining, rich loamy soil with compost and pH 6.2–7.0.
fertilizer: Balanced 5-10-10 or tomato feed with magnesium every 2 weeks after flowering.
pruning: Pinch early flowers to encourage bushy growth; stake heavy fruit-bearing branches.
common_problems: Bacterial leaf spot, blossom end rot, sunscald on fruit, aphids.

watering: Deep soak every 7–10 days during dry spells; mature trees need 1 inch of water weekly.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6–8 hours of uninterrupted sunlight.
soil: Well-drained loam to sandy loam with pH 6.0–7.0.
temperature: 10°C – 24°C (50°F – 75°F); requires winter chill hours (below 7°C) for dormancy.
fertilizer: Fruit tree fertilizer (10-10-10) in early spring; avoid late season nitrogen.
pruning: Prune dormant branches in winter/early spring to open tree canopy to sunlight.
common_problems: Apple scab fungus, cedar apple rust, codling moth, powdery mildew.
schedule_tuesday: Check leaf canopy for fungal spots 🔍
schedule_wednesday: Remove dead twigs or water sprouts ✂️

watering: High water demand: 1–1.5 inches weekly, especially during tasseling and silking stages.
sunlight: Full Sun: 8+ hours of direct bright sunlight.
soil: Warm, fertile, well-draining soil rich in organic matter with pH 5.8–6.8.
fertilizer: Heavy nitrogen feeder; apply nitrogen side-dressing when stalks reach knee-high.
pruning: No pruning required; weed carefully around shallow root systems.
common_problems: Corn earworms, rust fungus, leaf blight, smut galls.

watering: Deep, infrequent watering (every 10–14 days); let soil dry between waterings. Avoid wet vines.
sunlight: Full Sun: 7–8 hours of direct sunshine for sweet fruit development.
soil: Deep, loose, well-draining gravelly or sandy loam with pH 5.5–6.5.
temperature: 15°C – 32°C (60°F – 90°F). Warm, dry summers and mild winters.
fertilizer: Light balanced fertilizer in early spring; excess nitrogen causes vegetative overgrowth.
pruning: Heavy winter pruning of canes; summer canopy trimming to let sunlight hit fruit clusters.
common_problems: Black rot, downy mildew, powdery mildew, Japanese beetles.

watering: Keep evenly moist with 1 inch of water weekly. Water at the base to avoid crown rot.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6–10 hours of bright sunlight daily.
soil: Rich, slightly acidic, well-drained sandy loam with pH 5.5–6.8.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer (10-10-10) in spring; avoid excessive nitrogen during fruiting.
pruning: Pinch off runners (daughter plants) during first year to focus energy on roots and fruit.
common_problems: Gray mold (Botrytis), leaf spot, spider mites, slugs on berries.

watering: Water regularly during fruit formation (approx. 1 inch weekly); allow topsoil to dry slightly.
sunlight: Full Sun: 6–8 hours of direct sun for fruit color and sweetness.
soil: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam with pH 6.0–7.0.
fertilizer: Balanced 10-10-10 in early spring and again in early summer.
pruning: Open-center vase pruning in late winter to maximize air circulation and sunlight.
common_problems: Peach leaf curl (Taphrina deformans), brown rot, peach tree borer.

watering: Water every 1–2 weeks when the top 2 inches of soil feel completely dry. Drooping indicates thirst.
sunlight: Bright indirect light; tolerates medium to low light, avoid direct scorching sun.
soil: Well-draining indoor potting mix with perlite and peat moss.
temperature: 18°C – 30°C (65°F – 86°F). Protect from AC drafts and cold below 10°C.
fertilizer: Diluted balanced liquid houseplant fertilizer once a month during spring/summer.
pruning: Trim long vining stems to encourage bushier growth; wipe leaves with damp cloth.
common_problems: Root rot from overwatering, yellowing leaves, mealybugs, leggy vines from low light.

watering: Water very sparingly; once every 2–4 weeks. Soil must dry out 100% between waterings.
sunlight: Adaptable: thrives in indirect light, tolerates low light and partial direct sun.
soil: Cactus or succulent potting mix with coarse sand and pumice for quick drainage.
fertilizer: Feed once in spring and once in summer with mild succulent fertilizer (10-10-10).
pruning: Rarely needed; simply cut damaged outer leaves at soil line with sterile blade.
common_problems: Root rot from overwatering (mushy leaves), brown dry tips from underwatering.
schedule_monday: Check soil dryness (water only if bone dry) 💧
schedule_wednesday: Rotate pot 90 degrees for even light ☀️

watering: Water deeply but infrequently (every 3 weeks). Allow soil to dry completely.
sunlight: Bright direct to strong indirect sunlight for 6 hours daily.
soil: Sandy, gritty succulent or cactus mix with excellent drainage holes.
fertilizer: Rarely needed; feed once a year in spring with balanced water-soluble fertilizer.
pruning: Remove dry, brown, or dead outer leaves at the base. Harvest mature bottom leaves.
common_problems: Soft mushy leaves (overwatering), pale thin leaves (insufficient sun), scale insects.
schedule_monday: Light soak if pot is light and dry 💧
schedule_saturday: Check for soft spots at crown 🔍

watering: Water 1–2 inches weekly; water deeply at soil level in morning to prevent fungal mildew.
sunlight: Full Sun: At least 6 hours of direct sun daily for abundant blooms.
soil: Rich, well-draining loamy soil with plenty of compost, pH 6.0–6.5.
fertilizer: High phosphorus rose food or bone meal every 3–4 weeks during bloom cycle.
pruning: Deadhead spent blossoms weekly; hard prune in late winter to open bush center.
common_problems: Black spot fungus, powdery mildew, aphids, Japanese beetles, rust.
schedule_saturday: Spray neem oil if aphids present 🔍

watering: Water daily in summer or when topsoil feels dry. Do not let soil become waterlogged.
sunlight: Bright direct sunlight for 4–6 hours every day.
soil: Rich, loamy, well-drained soil with organic vermicompost, pH 6.0–7.5.
temperature: 20°C – 35°C (68°F – 95°F). Highly sensitive to cold and frost.
fertilizer: Organic vermicompost or cow dung manure once every month.
pruning: Pinch off flower buds (manjari) regularly to keep plant bushy and prevent seeding.
common_problems: Leaf spot, root rot from stagnant water, spider mites, cold wilt.

watering: Water every 1–2 weeks; allow top 2–3 inches of soil to dry out between waterings.
sunlight: Medium to bright indirect sunlight; avoid direct harsh sun which scorches leaves.
soil: Chunky, well-aerated potting mix containing bark, peat moss, and perlite.
fertilizer: Balanced 20-20-20 houseplant fertilizer diluted to half strength monthly in growing season.
pruning: Prune old lower leaves; train aerial roots into soil or onto a moss pole.
common_problems: Yellow leaves (overwatering), brown crispy fenestrations (low humidity), thrips.
schedule_wednesday: Tuck aerial roots into moss pole 🌿

watering: Water moderately; once a week. Keep soil slightly moist during summer, dry in winter.
sunlight: Bright indirect light; tolerates moderate shade. Avoid direct sun.
soil: Standard well-draining potting soil with good aeration, pH 6.0–7.0.
fertilizer: Feed monthly during spring and summer with weak liquid houseplant food.
pruning: Prune brown leaf tips and propagate plantlets ('spiderettes') in water or soil.
common_problems: Brown leaf tips (fluoride/chlorine in tap water or dry air), root rot.
schedule_monday: Water with filtered or rested water 💧
schedule_wednesday: Trim brown tips with clean shears ✂️
